audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0],[1],[3],[4],[5],[6].side read 'Skill' (and [3] read 'Skill' where it should stay) against content win[] and packet.levelChart, which both read Azir, Azir, Azir, Skill, Azir, Azir, Azir. Six rows disagreed across layers.
audit.why: Content and packet agree and the full-layer .why prose was already Azir-positive. It is also right: Ryze has no dash and every root he casts needs him inside 615, against a champion who farms from 740 through soldiers. Level 4-5 is genuinely the even stage — that is when his mana supports the Flux-Overload chain.
audit.corrected: phases[0],[1],[4],[5],[6].side -> Azir, phases[3].side -> Skill, with every .why in the group rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes named no Ryze timing, and the page treated level 6 as a dive threat from him.
audit.why: Realm Warp is 180/160/140s and creates a portal up to 3000 units away that teleports allies after a delay — it is a map/teamfight tool, not a gap-closer or a duel spike. Azir's spikes are Nashor's Tooth and Emperor's Divide (120/105/90s).
audit.corrected: breakdown.spikes, phases[4].why, dontsFull[2].d and content spikes[1].text now describe Realm Warp accurately.

audit.whatIsWrong: TWO fabricated mechanics were shipped on this matchup. (1) The content layer repeatedly refers to 'his E dash' and 'flash-E onto you' and calls Realm Warp 'Ryze's only gap-closer' — Ryze has NO dash in his kit. Spell Flux is an orb that debuffs. (2) content early/whys[0] claim 'Ryze's Q range is shorter than your soldier zone' — Overload is 1000 range and a Sand Soldier reaches 740, so it is the other way round.
audit.why: Riot's text: E 'releases an orb of pure magical power that damages an enemy and debuffs all nearby enemies'; R 'creates a portal to a nearby location. After a few seconds, allies standing near the portal are teleported'. Neither moves Ryze onto you. The decisive real interaction the page never stated: Rune Prison slows, and ROOTS only 'if the target has Flux on it' — so Spell Flux landing is the tell that the root is live, and his other basic abilities reset Overload's cooldown, which is why the chain arrives fast.
audit.corrected: The dash removed from whys[4], spikes[1].text, content mid and wants.you[1]; the range claim corrected in whys[0] and content early; the Flux-then-root sequencing written into winCon, tradeBad, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and phases[1].why.

audit.why: Rune Prison 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 at 615 range, Spell Flux 3.5/3.25/3/2.75/2.5, Overload 5 base and reset by his other spells, Realm Warp 180/160/140, Shifting Sands 22/20.5/19/17.5/16.
audit.corrected: Numbers now in breakdown.cooldowns, with the reset behaviour named as the reason the chain lands quickly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two COPY_PASTE_BLEED bullets: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim under 'Stand outside his answer while soldiers poke', dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under 'Shove past river without flank wards'.
audit.why: Both bodies answered a different question than their titles asked.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the 1000-vs-615 range band, and with what Realm Warp actually does to an unwarded river.

notes: CHART: phases[0],[1],[4],[5],[6].side were the stale token 'Skill' against content win[] and packet.levelChart, which both read Azir for those rows and 'Skill' only at Levels 4-5. phases[2] was already Azir and phases[3] was already Skill, so no edit was needed there. Full layer moved onto the content layer; no paired win[N] edit exists to propose because win[N] is already correct on disk for every row I touched, and each moved row's .why was rewritten in this same proposal. Ratings untouched. TWO FABRICATED MECHANICS REMOVED, both in the content layer and both shipped live: the page described an 'E dash' and a 'flash-E onto you' all-in and called Realm Warp 'Ryze's only gap-closer' — Ryze has no dash whatsoever, Spell Flux is a debuff orb and Realm Warp is a delayed team portal; and it claimed 'Ryze's Q range is shorter than your soldier zone' when Overload is 1000 against a 740 soldier. The genuine interaction that replaces both: Rune Prison slows, and only roots if Spell Flux is already on the target, so the Flux landing is the tell. Deliberately unasserted: whether a Sand Soldier can body-block Overload (it is flagged projectile and stops on the first enemy struck, but whether soldiers count as that enemy is not in Riot's text).
